S1.text: Black Friday has a clever trick. It can make spending feel like saving. Today, Alex heads into the sales with a three hundred dollar budget and two very different plans. One plan ends at three hundred and forty-one dollars. The other ends at two hundred and sixty-three. Same shop, same sales, seventy-eight dollars apart. Along the way, you'll get five simple rules for your own Black Friday, and none of them say never buy anything. Let's see what happens.

S2.text: Meet Alex. Alex isn't reckless. Alex has a holiday budget of three hundred dollars, and it has to cover a few things that genuinely need buying. A winter coat. A gift for a friend. And a phone charger that only works if you hold it at just the right angle. Waiting for Black Friday is a perfectly sensible plan. Sales can be real. The trouble usually isn't the sale. It's what the sale does to our decisions.

S3.text: Rule one: write the list before the sales start. Alex's list has three items. The coat is one hundred and twenty dollars, and it's twenty-five percent off, so ninety. The gift is sixty dollars, twenty percent off, so forty-eight. The charger is twenty-five dollars, twenty percent off, so twenty. Altogether that's one hundred and fifty-eight dollars, instead of two hundred and five. A real saving of forty-seven dollars on things Alex was already going to buy. That's Black Friday working the way it should.
